differences.what: Port trim: B's satin-silver flange (L 147-185) stands apart from the black throat and shows the curve of the tube wall inside, so it reads as machined trim with real depth. A's graphite flange (L 76-118) runs into the throat and the whole port reads as one heavy dark disc, with no clear step between flange and tube.

Background: A's grey sweep darkens unevenly, from 176 at top centre to 91 in the bottom-right corner against 127 bottom-left. That leaves a muddy, dark lower-right corner. B's warm seamless stays within 154-189 and is cleaner.

Brand red: A's 'OPEN OTHER SIDE' fin is washed out to a milky pink (RGB 190/68/72), and its slope sits dE 2.9 off the brand red. B keeps the fin saturated (180/41/41) and the slope on brand at dE 1.6.

Logo: A's gunmetal 'earmilk' sits about 78 levels below the face (median 167 vs 245) and reads crisply as a metal badge. B's pale, slightly pink warm-grey logo (median 193) looks washed out at full size.
Gable gloss: A's red slope carries a broad soft-box sheen that falls from 103 to 70 down the face; B's slope barely changes (86 to 71) and reads as flat plastic.
Body edge: on A the carton's right edge has a turning shade band (L about 205-213) inside the rim highlight; on B the band is about 226-236, so A's body looks slightly more three-dimensional.
